facts.fact: 夜店外 Julie 点烟：所以这才是你要打听死人公寓的原因——她倾向把问题看成系统性而非个人的，因此不必细说丧恸也能解释为何追查这家公司。
facts.anchor: Julie exhaled a line of smoke like in the movies. “Okay, so that’s why you wanted to know about dead people’s apartments.”

facts.fact: Julie 不擅长情绪对话：Mark 死后没问她要不要聊、需不需要什么——只是一直打电话、照旧贫嘴；不同朋友不同需要。
facts.anchor: She wasn’t big on emotional conversations, hadn’t asked me if I wanted to talk after Mark died or if I needed anything. She just kept calling, kept yapping like always. Different friends, different needs.

facts.fact: 法律上几乎没有追索：她讲有个客户在公寓做 Santería 被控轻罪；「驱魔算犯罪吗」——「轻罪」。
上楼时她想起 Mark 每上一层都要停；进屋后 Julie 摸光头、拿起 François 幸存的小镜子照唇——「只是口红」。
facts.anchor: She smiled but didn’t look at me. She picked up a small mirror on the table—one of François’s that survived—and touched her pinky to the bow of her lips.

facts.fact: 轮到她喝酒：她招认——她曾把「鬼警察」叫到 François 身上。
facts.anchor: It was my turn for a shot. I let it burn. “I called the ghost cops on François.”

facts.fact: Julie 反应：人都会搞砸，这是难免的——你后来做了什么？（她答：把他找回来、放出来。）
facts.anchor: “People fuck up,” Julie said. “That’s inevitable. What did you do after that?”

facts.fact: 她说明：公司在西边肉联厂区有仓库，把鬼关在冷冻柜的笼子里。
facts.anchor: “They have a warehouse on the west side, where all the meatpacking plants are. They store the ghosts in cages in a freezer.”

facts.fact: Julie 的怒火：鬼警察居然有鬼监狱；她追问：你和他们都能看见四处飘的鬼吗？
facts.anchor: “You mean the ghost cops have a fucking ghost jail?” There was a fire behind her eyes now.

facts.fact: 她判断：他们其实看不见鬼——否则就得承认；他们做这行是因为怕鬼。
facts.anchor: I don’t think these guys really see them, because then they’d have to admit it. I think they’re doing what they’re doing because they’re scared of them.”

facts.fact: 她讲完 Mary Ellen 的旧事（跳图书馆）后，Julie 举杯：敬 Mary Ellen，一饮而尽。
她的解释：能看见他们，同时也知道他们不在那儿——像光线的把戏；Julie 讲她妈以为在叔叔药店外见过祖母。
facts.anchor: It’s like you can see them, but somehow you also know they aren’t really there. It’s kinda like a trick of the light.”

facts.fact: Julie 递烟她拒了；她总拒（除非玩得很嗨），因为怕开始就停不下来；母亲的老话：别信任何说「第一支免费」的人。
facts.anchor: Plus, I never got what my mother used to say when I was little out of my head: Don’t trust anyone who says the first one’s free.

facts.fact: Julie 定性：这不是阴谋问题，而是「城市到底为谁而建」的哲学问题——她答：你是说谁受益。
facts.anchor: “It’s a philosophical issue, you know? Who is a city really for?”

facts.fact: Julie 的楼市分析：旧社会服务换成给地产商的税收减免；「有计划的萎缩」比 Robert Moses 更狠——地铁、学校、医院、消防任其烂掉，社区自行清算。
facts.anchor: Who needs Robert Moses,” she started yelling, “when you got planned shrinkage! Let the subways go to shit, the schools, the hospitals, the fucking…the fucking fire department—the neighborhoods liquidate themselves.”

facts.fact: Julie 谈 Claude：总处理痛苦的人会习惯它——不是习惯而是被吸引，不想要轻松的东西。
facts.anchor: But I think that if you deal with pain all the time, you get used to it. Or, not used to it. Attracted to it. You don’t want something easy.”

facts.fact: 她的公寓宣言：搬进此处时 Mark 刚与父母断绝、她在此悼母；两人不是家人而是朋友——那对她更重要。
facts.anchor: We weren’t family—we were friends, which meant more to me.

facts.fact: 她逐件整理母亲遗物直到只剩必留的（唱片、锅、墨西哥刺绣裙、Frankenthaler）；那些东西提醒她：母亲已不再需要它们。
facts.anchor: Everything my mother left behind was a reminder that she didn’t need it anymore.

facts.fact: 结尾：她掀开皮箱（母亲从 Lvov 带来的steamer trunk，被当茶几）——想起 Mark 哭着说不想被锁进箱子里——于是把箱盖猛地掀到地板，把裙子、毯子、照片全扔出来，只为确认。
facts.anchor: And then I remembered him crying that he didn’t want to be locked in a box, and I threw the lid open so hard that it smacked the floor. I threw the dress to the ground, the extra blankets and photographs and other items of hers that weren’t mine, until the trunk was empty, just to make sure.
